title: Autonomous Tuner: Rollout orchestration for Optimize suggestions
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Goal: Build a safe, policy-driven orchestration layer to auto-apply Optimize batching/caching suggestions with gated rollouts, canary evaluation, and approval hooks. Scope: - Implement a rollout controller that executes suggestion changes (batch_size, cache TTL, kv-prefix caching, quantization profile) against tenant groups in stages. - Define canary cohorts (percentile-based and traffic-based) and multi-metric evaluation windows (p95 latency, cost per token, error rate, quality delta from eval set). - Integrate human approval gates for high-risk suggestions (quality-impacting or >10% expected cost change). - Provide dry-run and simulation mode producing expected unit economics and predicted latency distribution. Success metrics: - No customer-facing latency regressions above +10% p95 for canary cohorts. - Automated rollback triggered within 10 minutes after threshold breach. - Reduction in manual approvals for low-risk suggestions to <20% after release. Constraints: - Must work across Hosted and Dedicated deployments; private customers with strict RBAC must see proposals but not be auto-applied without org approval. - Runtime must avoid blocking serving paths; use async workers to apply config changes. Acceptance criteria: 1) Rollout controller can apply suggestion to a 5% traffic canary, observe metrics for a configurable window, and either ramp to 100% or rollback automatically. 2) Approval rule engine supports expression-based policies (e.g., "quality_drop > 0.5% AND cost_saving > 8% => require_approval"). 3) Console UI shows staged rollout progress, canary metrics, and one-click rollback/override. 4) Audit log contains before/after config, who/what triggered change, and rollback reason. Out-of-scope for this ticket: full RBAC UI for Private (will be follow-up), and advanced ML-based quality prediction (P0 for later cycle).
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: Reviewed PRD with PM/Research. Agreed to prioritize reliability first: controller must allow safe aborts and be observable. Action: prototype controller API and metrics hooks. — Aisha

2026-03-03 - Design sync: Decided on two canary strategies: traffic-percent canaries and user-cohort canaries (tenant-tag based). We will default to traffic-percent and add cohort selector later. Need instrumentation for per-cohort p95 and cost. — Mateo

2026-03-04 - Engineering note: Built initial rollout-controller skeleton (k8s-style phases: Pending -> Canary -> Evaluate -> Ramp -> Complete/Abort). Using Redis-backed state to avoid leader election complexity for MVP. Draft PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287 — Mateo

2026-03-05 - Metrics: Hooked up canary telemetry to console ingest. Dashboard tile: optimize/canary/ENG-33210 shows latency, token-cost, quality-regression. Ran internal dry-run on staging with synthetic traffic; observed expected cost drop of 9% and p95 change +3%. — SRE (Jordan)

2026-03-06 - PM feedback: Add explicit human-approval policy for suggestions that alter quantization profile or have model-parameter changes. Also require a mandatory dry-run report be attached to approval for any >7% cost change. — Lina (PM)

2026-03-07 - Security review scheduled: Ensure audit trail cannot be tampered with; plan to append immutable entries to event-store and surface signed snapshots to console. Ticket ENG-34102 created for audit-store hardening. — Aisha

2026-03-08 - Blocker discovered: Some Dedicated deployments do not expose the per-tenant metrics due to legacy sidecar; workaround is to use sampled traces for canary detection. Marking an implementation dependency on ENG-24652. Plan: Implement traffic-percent canaries for MVP and add cohort detection in follow-up. — Mateo
